questions.stem: Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are animals. Conclusion: All cats are animals. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.explanation: Basic transitive chain: A ⊆ D ⊆ E → A ⊆ E. Classic A + A → A Barbara syllogism.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statements: Some pens are pencils. All pencils are books. Which conclusion follows? (1) Some pens are books. (2) All books are pencils.
questions.explanation: Some pens are pencils (subset overlap). All pencils are books → the overlap lies inside books → 'Some pens are books' is valid (I + A → I). Conclusion 2 reverses an 'All' statement, which is invalid.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statements: No teacher is a doctor. Some doctors are engineers. Which of the following conclusions definitely follows?
questions.explanation: E (No teacher is a doctor) + I (Some doctors are engineers) → O (Some engineers are not teachers): the doctor-engineers overlap cannot be teachers (because no teacher is a doctor). Hence at least those engineers are not teachers. Other conclusions are not forced.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red. Conclusion: Some roses MAY be red. (Is this a POSSIBILITY conclusion?)

options.option_text: It follows as a DEFINITE conclusion

questions.explanation: POSSIBILITY syllogism (banking-mains style): 'some roses MAY be red' — the premises neither ESTABLISH nor REFUTE this, so it is a valid possibility. The same premises do NOT support a DEFINITE 'some roses are red' conclusion. cannot be ruled out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

_fixes.was: It follows as a POSSIBILITY (cannot be ruled out)

questions.stem: Statements: (i) All politicians are orators. (ii) Some orators are liars. (iii) No liar is a philosopher. Which follows? (a) Some politicians are not philosophers. (b) Some orators are not philosophers.
questions.explanation: (ii) + (iii): Some orators are liars; no liar is a philosopher → those orator-liars are not philosophers → 'Some orators are not philosophers' (b) is valid. (a) requires bringing politicians into the chain via (i) — but we don't know if any politicians ARE the orators who are liars. So (a) does not definitely follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All pens are books. All books are stationery.
Conclusions: I. All pens are stationery. II. Some stationery are pens.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All P→B→S ⟹ All P are S. Particular conversion: Some S are P. Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No dog is a cat. All cats are animals.
Conclusions: I. No dog is an animal. II. Some animals are not dogs.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: No D is C, All C are A. Dogs and cats are disjoint. Conc I is wrong (dogs can be animals via other paths). Conc II follows: cats are animals and no cat is a dog, so some animals are not dogs.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some chairs are tables. All tables are furniture.
Conclusions: I. Some chairs are furniture. II. All furniture are chairs.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Some C are T, All T→F ⟹ Some C are F (Darii). Conc II reverses universal — invalid. Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All mangoes are fruits. No fruit is a vegetable.
Conclusions: I. No mango is a vegetable. II. Some vegetables are mangoes.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All M→F, No F is V ⟹ No M is V. Conc I follows. Conc II contradicts Conc I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some birds are parrots. No parrot is a crow.
Conclusions: I. Some birds are not crows. II. All crows are birds.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Some B are P, No P is C ⟹ Some B (the parrots) are not C. Conc I follows. Conc II has no support.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All apples are red. All red things are beautiful.
Conclusions: I. All apples are beautiful. II. Some beautiful things are apples.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All A→R→B. Both Barbara chain and particular conversion hold. Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All cats are mammals. All dogs are mammals.
Conclusions: I. All cats are dogs. II. Some cats are dogs.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Both are subsets of mammals but no direct C-D link exists. Neither follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All roses are flowers. All flowers are plants. All plants are living things.
Conclusions: I. All roses are living things. II. Some living things are roses.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Triple chain R→F→P→L. Both Conc I and its particular conversion follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some teachers are writers. All writers are intelligent.
Conclusions: I. Some teachers are intelligent. II. Some intelligent people are teachers.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Some T→W, All W→I ⟹ Some T are I (Darii). Particular conversion: Some I are T. Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No star is a planet. All planets are celestial bodies.
Conclusions: I. No star is a celestial body. II. Some celestial bodies are not stars.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Stars and planets are disjoint, but stars may independently be celestial bodies. Conc I too strong. Conc II: planets are celestial bodies and no planet is a star → some celestial bodies are not stars.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some balls are red. All red things are circles.
Conclusions: I. Some balls are circles. II. All circles are red.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Some B→R, All R→C ⟹ Some B are C (Darii). Conc II reverses universal — invalid. Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No stone is gold. All gold is metal.
Conclusions: I. No stone is metal. II. Some metals are not stones.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Stones and gold are disjoint, but stones may independently be metals (like iron). Conc I invalid. Conc II: gold is metal and no gold is stone → some metals are not stones.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some files are folders. No folder is a drive.
Conclusions: I. Some files are drives. II. No file is a drive.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: Some F are Fd, No Fd is Dr. Files that are folders are not drives. Other files may or may not be drives — neither conclusion is certain.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All books are novels. No novel is a poem. Some poems are songs.
Conclusions: I. No book is a poem. II. Some songs are not novels.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All B→N, No N is P ⟹ No B is P (I). Some P are S, No N is P ⟹ Some S are not N (II). Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some cars are buses. Some buses are trucks.
Conclusions: I. Some cars are trucks. II. No car is a truck.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Either I or II follows (complementary pair)

questions.explanation: Two 'Some' premises yield no definite conclusion. Either I or II must be true (complementary pair).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All phones are gadgets. Some gadgets are expensive.
Conclusions: I. Some phones are expensive. II. Some expensive things are gadgets.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All P→G, Some G are E. Expensive gadgets may not be phones → Conc I invalid. Some G are E → Some E are G by conversion. Only II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No tree is a shrub. No shrub is a herb.
Conclusions: I. No tree is a herb. II. Some herbs are trees.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Two negative premises → no valid conclusion. Rule: at least one premise must be affirmative.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All rivers are water bodies. All water bodies are natural resources. Some natural resources are renewable.
Conclusions: I. All rivers are natural resources. II. Some renewable resources are rivers.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All R→WB→NR → Conc I follows. Renewable NRs may not be rivers → Conc II doesn't follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All politicians are speakers. Some teachers are speakers.
Conclusions: I. Some teachers are politicians. II. All speakers are politicians.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Undistributed middle (speakers not distributed in either premise). No valid conclusion.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All doctors are graduates. No graduate is uneducated.
Conclusions: I. No doctor is uneducated. II. All uneducated people are non-graduates.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All D→G, No G is U ⟹ No D is U (I). No G is U ↔ All G are non-U; contrapositive: All U are non-G = all uneducated are non-graduates (II). Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some students are not hardworking. All hardworking people succeed.
Conclusions: I. Some students do not succeed. II. All students succeed.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Some S not H. All H→Succeed. Non-hardworking students: premises don't say they fail. Conc II contradicts first premise possibility. Neither definite.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles are quadrilaterals. No quadrilateral is a circle.
Conclusions: I. No square is a circle. II. All squares are quadrilaterals.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All Sq→Rect→Quad, No Quad is Circle ⟹ No Sq is Circle (I). All Sq→Quad from chain (II). Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some politicians are honest. No honest person is corrupt.
Conclusions: I. Some politicians are not corrupt. II. All corrupt people are politicians.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Some P are H, No H is C ⟹ Some P are not C (Festino). Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some scientists are poets. Some poets are musicians.
Conclusions: I. Some scientists are musicians. II. No scientist is a musician.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Two particular premises → no definite conclusion. Neither follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No doctor is a lawyer. Some lawyers are engineers.
Conclusions: I. Some engineers are not doctors. II. No engineer is a doctor.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: No D is L. Some L are E → Some E are L; No D is L → Some E (those = lawyers) are not D. Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All keys open locks. Some locks are antique.
Conclusions: I. Some antique things are keys. II. All antique things are keys.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All K→L, Some L are A. Antique locks needn't be keys (keys are locks but not all locks are keys). Neither follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All tigers are animals. Some animals are wild. All wild things are dangerous.
Conclusions: I. Some animals are dangerous. II. Some tigers are dangerous.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Some A are W, All W→D ⟹ Some A are D (I). For II: All T are A but dangerous animals may not overlap with tigers. Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: No examiner is lenient.
Conclusions: I. All examiners are strict. II. Some lenient people are not examiners.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: No E is L → No L is E (conversion) → All L are non-E → Some L are not E (II). 'Strict' ≠ 'non-lenient' without extra premise → I invalid.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All artists are creative. All creative people are productive.
Conclusions: I. All productive people are artists. II. Some productive people are artists.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All A→C→P. Conc I reverses universal (invalid). Conc II: Some P are A by particular conversion. Only II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some hills are mountains. All mountains are snow-capped.
Conclusions: I. Some hills are snow-capped. II. All snow-capped things are mountains.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Some H→M, All M→SC ⟹ Some H are SC (Darii). Conc II reverses universal. Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No farmer is illiterate. Some illiterate people are poor.
Conclusions: I. Some poor people are not farmers. II. All farmers are literate.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: No F is I → Some P (who are I) are not F (I). No F is I ↔ All F are non-illiterate = literate (II). Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All A are B. All B are C. No C is D.
Conclusions: I. No A is D. II. Some D are not B.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: All A→B→C, No C is D ⟹ No A is D (I). No C is D → No D is C; All B→C so All D are non-B ⟹ Some D are not B (II). Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All judges are lawyers. Some lawyers are professors. No professor is a businessman.
Conclusions: I. Some judges are not businessmen. II. Some professors are judges.
Which follow?
questions.explanation: All J→L. Some L are P: judges may or may not be the professor-lawyers. Conc II not guaranteed. Conc I: all judges are lawyers, and no path makes judges businessmen → no judge is a businessman → some judges are not businessmen. Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some books are pens. All pens are erasers. Some erasers are sharpeners. No sharpener is a ruler.
Conclusions: I. Some books are erasers. II. No pen is a ruler. III. Some sharpeners are books.
Which follow?
questions.explanation: Some Bk→P, All P→E ⟹ Some Bk are E (I ✓). All P→E, Some E are Sh, No Sh is R → no pen is ruler (II ✓). Some Bk are E, Some E are Sh: two 'some' chains don't guarantee overlap (III ✗). I and II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All students who study hard pass. Ram did not pass.
Conclusions: I. Ram did not study hard. II. Ram is not a student.
Which follow?
questions.explanation: Study hard → Pass. Contrapositive: Not Pass → Not Study Hard. Ram didn't pass → Ram didn't study hard (I). Ram could be a student who didn't study hard → II invalid.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No lazy person is successful. All successful people are happy.
Conclusions: I. No lazy person is happy. II. Some unhappy people are lazy.
Which follow?
questions.explanation: No Lazy is Successful. All Successful→Happy. Lazy people could independently be happy via other means. Conc I too strong. Conc II: unhappy people include failed hardworking people too. Neither definite.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All lions are brave. Some brave animals are tigers.
Conclusions: I. Some tigers are lions. II. All lions are tigers.
Which follow?
questions.explanation: All L→B, Some B are T. The brave tigers may not be lions. No L-T link guaranteed. Neither follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All pens are keys. All keys are locks. Some locks are heavy.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are heavy (definite). II. All pens being heavy is a possibility.
Which is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All P→K→L. Some L are H — the heavy locks may not be pens. Conc I (definite) invalid. All pens are locks; it is possible all locks are heavy → Conc II (possibility) holds.
questions.subject: Reasoning
